forecaster_note: "We're lacking new energy and this mixture of small wind swells will only be giving us a few waist to stomach high options. Aim for the morning low tide and pack some floaty shortboards, logs or foamies to make the most of it. The arvo will see a few less options as some banks fill in although it should be clean as NW offshores are hanging around." — Surfline Sydney forecast team. Agent read: 43 kJ this morning is thin but clean, and the 50° NE angle sits inside Dee Why's window — it just has no period behind it at 6 seconds. Saturday is the flattest day on the chart at 19 kJ. Sunday is the week: energy jumps to 221 kJ (peaking 366) on a 4.4ft 9-second swell, but it arrives from 184° — dead south — so Long Reef and the south-facing corners will get it and Dee Why will not.

wind.summary: Light NNW–WNW offshore from dawn through midday, going soft E onshore after 3pm.

shark.summary: SharkSmart NSW feed live this morning (latest statewide detection Thu 3:19pm, Hungry Head). No Northern Beaches detections in the last 24 hours — most recent local was Warriewood, Wed 19 Aug 7am.

days.label: Today
days.note: Small, clean and weak — 43 kJ average on a 3.1ft NE windswell at just 6 seconds. Offshore holds until about 3pm, so a mid-morning session on the run-in off the 7:39am low is the play. Long Reef and Curl Curl are holding the most size.

dee-why.window: 9–11:30am on the pushing tide off the 7:39am low, while the WNW offshore still holds.

tip.label: Dee Why Point — frontside rights
tip.text: The 50° NE angle is right in your window, but at 6 seconds and 43 kJ there's no punch behind it. Sit wide on the Point for the set waves rather than fighting the shorebreak. Frontside, so keep it high-line and fast — this is a day for speed, not power.

long-reef.window: 8–11am. Best-rated of the four — picks up more of the ESE component and the low-tide banks are the pick.

tip.label: Long Reef
tip.text: Rated FAIR while Dee Why sits poor-to-fair. Same 43 kJ, so paddle speed and wave selection beat board volume here. Worth the extra walk this morning.

curl-curl.window: 8:30–11am off the low. South corner is cleanest under the WNW.

tip.label: Curl Curl
tip.text: Matching Long Reef on size and rating. Backside on the lefts down the beach — the NE angle feeds the south end first.

manly.window: Marginal — North Steyne banks only, tight around the 7:39am low.

tip.label: North Steyne
tip.text: Weakest of the four today. Only worth it if you're already south — otherwise Long Reef or Curl Curl for the same drive.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The flattest day on the chart — 19 kJ average, knee-to-thigh at best. WSW offshore in the morning, going cross-shore SSW after lunch. Log, high-volume board, or leave it and rest up for Sunday.

dee-why.window: 6:30–9:30am either side of the 8:46am low. The SSW cross-shore kills it after lunch.
alerts: Smallest energy of the week — 19 kJ average

long-reef.window: Around the 8:46am low — best of a weak bunch, but still only knee-to-thigh.

manly.window: Not worth the drive — rated POOR through the morning.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is a throwaway at 19 kJ. Sunday is the session: a 4.4ft 9-second groundswell fills in mid-morning and energy jumps to 221 kJ, peaking near 366. The catch is the angle — 184°, dead south, which wraps badly into Dee Why. Long Reef goes chest-to-overhead and fair-to-good. NE onshores arrive Sunday afternoon, so be in the water by 8am.

dee-why.window: Sunday 8–11am. Expect roughly half the size of Long Reef — the dead-S angle doesn't get in here.
alerts: Sun: 184° swell is Dee Why's worst angle — heavy size loss

long-reef.window: Sunday 8–11am — the standout session of the week. Chest-to-overhead sets as the tide runs out.
alerts: Biggest of the four on Sunday — 366 kJ peak

curl-curl.window: Sunday mid-morning. South corner holds the cleanest shape before the NE fills in.

manly.window: Sunday only, and it's the most shadowed of the four from a dead-south swell.
